item.title: Optoma UHZ36 Projector Offers Bright 4K Image with Limited Features
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Optoma UHZ36 Review: Light on Features, But Lumens Aplenty
The Optoma UHZ36 is a 4K home entertainment projector designed for bright, watchable images in ambient light. It lacks built-in streaming capabilities or a bundled dongle, requiring users to add a third-party device via HDMI. Priced at $1,599 (often lower), it offers 3,500 ISO lumens of brightness, a 30,000-hour lifespan in Eco mode, and a laser-phosphor light source that produces four primary colors using a blue laser and color wheel. The six-segment color wheel (clear, red, two greens, two yellows) reduces rainbow artifacts compared to four-segment models. While it delivers sharp images with good shadow detail for SDR and HDR content, its color gamut is smaller than triple-laser models, avoiding laser speckle issues. The projector measures 4.6 by 14.4 by 9.6 inches and weighs 7.5 pounds, suitable for portable or semi-permanent setups. It includes two HDMI 2.0 ports, a USB-A port for power, and a 15-watt mono speaker for basic audio. For optimal performance, users must adjust color saturation, black levels, and disable frame interpolation. HDR support is limited to HDR10, and the projector lacks 3D support. Input lag measures 117.2ms for 1080p/60Hz, which is high for gaming, though 4K/60Hz lag is 57.3ms. The UHZ36 excels in brightness, delivering a bright image on a 90-inch screen in a dark room, but its default color settings can appear faded with disc-based content. Competitors like the Epson Home Cinema 2350 and BenQ W2720i offer vertical lens shift and integrated streaming dongles, making them more versatile for certain setups. The UHZ36 is best suited for casual viewing in lit environments, with trade-offs in color gamut and connectivity features.

item.title: Super Mario 64 Plaque's Text May Finally Be Revealed
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: We might finally know what's written on that mysterious plaque in Super Mario 64
A programmer has used computational analysis to suggest the text on a mysterious plaque in Super Mario 64 may finally be deciphered. The plaque, which has puzzled fans for 30 years, was analyzed by Mochi64 using open-source software to match pixel patterns with potential text combinations. The result indicates the top of the plaque reads 'Eternal Star' and the bottom reads 'We hope so.' These phrases are considered the closest match from millions of tested combinations, though the software does not confirm absolute accuracy. Previous theories, such as 'L is Real 2401' suggesting Luigi's hidden presence, gained traction in the 1990s and were revived when Shigeru Miyamoto mentioned the game's team experimented with a two-player mode. An early build showing Mario and Luigi in a bare room further fueled speculation. Nintendo has not officially confirmed the findings, leaving the plaque's message unresolved. The analysis highlights the plaque's possible connection to the game's star-collecting mechanic, with 'Eternal Star' aligning with the star statue nearby. Despite the breakthrough, definitive verification remains uncertain.

item.title: Repurpose Old USB Cables Instead of Throwing Them Away
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your old USB charging cables — Repurpose them instead
Old USB cables can be repurposed instead of discarded. Many still conduct electricity despite being outdated, making them useful for DIY projects or small electronics. Cables with intact wiring can power LED lights, sensors, or serve as garden twine, plant hangers, or craft materials like coasters, keychains, and wire art. The copper core and plastic sheathing are valuable materials, though frayed cables pose fire risks if reused for power. The UN's Global E-waste Monitor 2024 reported 69 million tons of e-waste globally in 2022, with only 22.3% properly recycled. Repurposing extends cable lifespan and reduces demand for new manufacturing. Retailers like Best Buy and Staples offer free recycling for old cables, while functional ones can be donated to schools or STEM programs. Creative reuse options include making travel charging kits, organizing charging stations, or converting cables into decorative items. Proper disposal through recycling is recommended when cables are no longer usable.

item.title: Polymarket faces scrutiny over inflated election trading volume
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Original headline: Post-Election Trading Puts Polymarket Volume Under Scrutiny
Polymarket’s Ethiopia and Romania election markets saw over $600 million in trading volume, much of it linked to losing candidates or disrupted processes. In Ethiopia, more than $41 million was wagered on Shimelis Abdisa, a non-winning candidate, while only $173,000 was bet on Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who secured a parliamentary majority. The Ethiopian market remained open for 123 days after the election, allowing repeated trades that inflated volume. MSR Decode found 98% of trades in the Ethiopian market resulted in no net gain, with contracts held for an average of nine seconds, suggesting artificial activity farming. In Romania, the 2024 presidential election was annulled, and Polymarket kept the original market open while a new one ran for the replacement vote. An algorithm flagged 99.6% of Romanian trades as suspicious wash trading, a practice prohibited by Polymarket’s terms. Rajiv Sethi, a Barnard College economics professor, noted that such activity could misrepresent genuine interest. Polymarket blocked accounts flagged for suspicious behavior but did not clarify why trades continued for so long. The CFTC has previously investigated potential manipulation on the platform, and the debate over market safeguards now includes how platforms monitor activity after events are effectively decided. The company, valued at $21 billion, faces scrutiny over whether its volume metrics reflect real trading or repetitive turnover.

item.title: Windows 11 Storage Sense Automates Cleanup Tasks
item.description:

Windows 11 Storage Sense automates storage cleanup tasks previously handled manually. The tool removes files from Downloads folders, marks OneDrive files as online-only, and allows custom retention thresholds. Users can configure cleanup schedules to run daily, weekly, or monthly, with options to delete Recycle Bin files or manage synced files based on inactivity periods. Storage Sense prioritizes system drive maintenance, avoiding other drives and app-specific caches. It complements Disk Cleanup for comprehensive cleanup but does not replace it. The tool helps prevent performance issues caused by low disk space, ensuring Windows updates and operations function properly. Users are advised to maintain at least 10% free space on the system drive. Storage Sense streamlines routine maintenance by handling tasks like temporary file deletion and folder organization, reducing manual intervention needed for storage management.

Apple updated its App Store guidelines to prohibit apps that use AI to generate offensive content or disguise themselves as non-offensive apps to bypass review. The changes require apps hosting user-generated content to filter objectionable material, allow reporting of offensive content, and let users block abusive accounts. Hidden or undocumented features, including apps that misrepresent their purpose during review and later reveal harmful capabilities like 'nudification,' are now banned. Apple will remove apps that add new features post-approval. The company also reinforced legal language to block apps promoting human trafficking and child exploitation. Last year, Apple blocked 150,000 apps and removed 193,000 developer accounts for fraud. In July, San Francisco ordered Apple and Google to delete nudification apps, accusing them of profiting from store fees. A Tech Transparency Project report in April found both stores hosted multiple nudify apps, some rated for minors. item.title: Capping FPS in Games Can Improve Performance and Reduce Tearing
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Should you limit your FPS in games? Here's when it makes sense
Capping frame rates in games can improve performance and reduce screen tearing. Gamers using high-end hardware should consider setting an FPS limit to maintain stable performance, lower GPU load, and prevent screen tearing when paired with V-Sync. A frame rate cap is especially beneficial on VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) monitors, as it keeps in-game action within the display's effective range, reducing latency. Screen tearing occurs when the GPU sends a new frame before the previous one is fully displayed, causing flickering lines. Capping FPS to three to four frames below a monitor's max refresh rate (e.g., 57 fps for 60Hz, 117 fps for 120Hz) prevents this issue. V-Sync synchronizes frame rates with the monitor's refresh rate but introduces input lag, typically one additional refresh cycle. NVIDIA's Fast V-Sync reduces this lag while minimizing tearing. To cap FPS, users can use GPU-specific software like NVIDIA Control Panel or AMD Adrenalin, or third-party tools like Guru3D RTSS RivaTuner. For VRR displays, setting a cap slightly below the max refresh rate helps reduce lag without noticeable performance loss. Gamers with powerful GPUs may not notice frame drops, ensuring smooth, tear-free gameplay.

item.title: Nvidia launches open AI models for enterprise agents and local PCs

item.title: Laser pointers can damage security cameras but require specific conditions
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why you should never point a laser pointer at a security camera
Laser pointers can damage security cameras, though it requires specific conditions. A 2021 case in Clearwater, Florida, saw a man arrested for targeting Scientology surveillance cameras with a laser, causing $2,000 in damages through dead spots on lenses. Lasers emit intense light that overwhelms camera sensors, leading to temporary blindness or permanent damage. Most CCTV cameras use CMOS or CCD sensors, which are vulnerable to sustained laser exposure. High-intensity lasers generate heat, creating dead pixels and dark spots. However, damaging modern cameras is difficult due to sensor protections and the challenge of maintaining steady aim. Researchers at IPVM found it nearly impossible to keep a laser focused on a camera from 5 feet away without hand movement. Vince Gilligan, co-creator of Better Call Saul, noted that the show’s laser trick would only work on 1960s-era cameras. While low-power lasers (under 5mW) cause only temporary glare, federal regulations prohibit selling such devices. Preventative measures include positioning cameras out of reach, using multiple overlapping cameras, and installing systems that detect light changes or unusual activity. Legal risks also exist, as targeting cameras is often illegal regardless of damage extent.

item.title: Embedded AI Evaluators Face Challenges, Hugging Face Chief Says
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Embedded AI evaluators won’t be an easy solution, Hugging Face’s policy chief says
AI labs rely on benchmarking to compare models, but methods remain inconsistent and evolving, according to Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer. During a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt, Solaiman emphasized that trust in current evaluations hinges on reproducibility and access to model data, with open weights playing a critical role. She noted that benchmarking is an 'evolving science' where comparisons between tests lack meaningful standards, and embedded evaluators—third-party observers placed within AI organizations—face skepticism over their neutrality. Anthropic’s decision to hire Accenture as an evaluator drew criticism, highlighting doubts about the qualifications of such firms. Evaluations are shifting from focusing solely on models to assessing the entire system, including tools like harnesses that influence performance. Solaiman warned that agentic evaluations are costly and underdeveloped, with more attention needed for holistic agent assessments. She concluded that the evaluation space lacks uniformity, and industry-wide standardization is essential for benchmarking to remain a reliable tool.

item.title: Privacy Concerns Cause Stress, Experts Offer Solutions
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Why Caring About Online Privacy Is Destroying Your Sanity (And 6 Steps to Get It Back)
Privacy fatigue is widespread as digital tracking and data collection become pervasive. Experts warn that constant exposure to surveillance tools, biometric scans, and ISP data sales create overwhelming pressure to manage personal data. Jason Ng from OpenVPN advises focusing on high-impact decisions, such as limiting app data access, rather than getting bogged down by minor choices. Chris Wallis of Intruder emphasizes the need for scalable processes to filter out noise from security alerts. Dr. Lorrie Cranor acknowledges that some fatigue is inevitable but recommends using plug-and-play tools like Ghostery and DuckDuckGo, along with a decision-making framework that defaults to privacy-protective settings. Neha Kochar of Firefox highlights the importance of choosing services with built-in data protections, noting a recent scam targeting her hotel booking data. The article outlines six automated strategies to reduce privacy fatigue, including installing tracker blockers like Privacy Badger and setting default privacy preferences. These steps aim to simplify digital interactions without requiring constant vigilance, allowing users to reclaim control over their data while minimizing daily decision fatigue.

item.title: Asus Ascent QN10 Lags Behind Mac mini in AI Performance
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Asus Ascent QN10 Review: This Climber Gets Grounded by the Mac mini
The Asus Ascent QN10 mini PC is positioned as an agentic AI tool with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, offering 80 TOPS AI processing via its Hexagon NPU. However, it lacks the fastest AI compute power among mini PCs, as AMD and Intel chips provide higher totals. The AMD Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 delivers 131 TOPS with integrated graphics, while Intel’s Core Ultra X7 358H combines 50 TOPS NPU with 122 TOPS from its GPU for 172 TOPS total. Qualcomm’s Adreno X2-90 GPU is noted as 1.5 times faster than the previous generation but does not contribute significantly to AI performance. The QN10’s 32GB LPDDR5X memory and 512GB NVMe SSD make it suitable for AI development on lower-end hardware, though more powerful apps require desktops with dedicated GPUs. The system measures 1.57 by 5.12 by 5.12 inches, with a quiet design and seven USB ports, including three USB4 connections. Competitors include the $1,299 Apple Mac mini (M6 chip), which outperforms the QN10 in single-threaded tasks, and the $2,799 Asus NUC 16 Pro Mini. Test results show the QN10 is competitive in some workloads but lags behind the Mac mini and HP Z2 Mini G1a in multi-threaded performance. Memory bandwidth differences, with the Mac mini’s M6 offering 170 GBps versus the QN10’s 152 GBps, may explain its superior AI performance. The QN10 remains a viable option for developers targeting similar devices but is not recommended for heavy AI workloads.

item.title: Ring Air Quality Monitor Tracks PM2.5, CO, But Misses VOCs
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Ring Air Quality Monitor Review: Smart, Simple Air Tracking, With One Omission
The Ring Air Quality Monitor ($69.99) tracks PM2.5, carbon monoxide, temperature, and humidity levels in homes. It lacks volatile organic compound (VOC) detection, unlike the Amazon Smart Air Quality Monitor ($69.99). The device resembles the Amazon model in size and design but uses Amazon Sidewalk for connectivity instead of Wi-Fi. It features a round LED indicator for status, with green for good air quality, yellow for poor, and blinking for updates. No audible alarms or display screen are included. The Ring app integrates with other Ring devices, offering hourly data charts, alert thresholds, and device settings. It supports Alexa voice commands and routines, allowing automation with smart home devices like air purifiers. During testing, it accurately detected PM2.5 levels comparable to more expensive monitors. While it does not clean air, it can trigger connected devices to improve conditions. The review rates it 5.0/5.0, calling it an exemplary, budget-friendly option for users already invested in the Ring ecosystem, though the Amazon model offers better value with VOC tracking.

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes documentary earns $15 million opening weekend

item.title: Disabling Microsoft apps on Windows 11 improves system performance

Microsoft apps on Windows 11 consume system resources, slowing performance. Disabling specific services improves speed. Microsoft Edge uses memory in the background, even when not active. item.title: AI Agents Threaten Internet Usability as Websites Block Them
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
AI agents like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse are causing widespread disruption on the internet. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September. Websites are blocking these agents, which act on behalf of users to perform tasks like booking flights or negotiating prices. Platforms like Amazon and Yelp have restricted AI agents, with Amazon waging a court battle against Perplexity to block its agents. A judge recently ruled in Perplexity’s favor, but Amazon has appealed, arguing AI agents threaten its advertising business by blurring the line between human and bot traffic. Ethan Mollick, a Wharton professor, warns that as agents become common, they will overwhelm customer service systems, frustrating human users. Shopify is already creating dedicated checkout lanes for agents to bypass human-centric interfaces. The internet, designed for people, may shift toward prioritizing agents, leading to worse experiences for humans. Websites could become less user-friendly, with verification systems requiring constant human proof, and prices varying based on agents’ identities. While agents can help with tasks like disputing medical bills or finding affordable insurance, their impact depends on rules governing their interactions. Some regulations, like protecting credit card data, will benefit all users, but contested rules—such as whether businesses can block agents—will shape whether the web serves humans or agents. The future remains uncertain as AI agents reshape the internet’s design.

item.title: Arm's AGI CPU Outperforms AMD EPYC 9755 in Agentic AI Benchmarks
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests
Arm claims its AGI CPU, designed for agentic AI workloads, delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack compared to AMD EPYC 9755, based on tests using a new evaluation methodology developed with Fujitsu, Meta, and OpenAI. The results, verified by an independent Signal65 analysis, show Arm’s AGI CPU outperforms AMD in five of seven workloads, with an average 20% per-chip advantage. At the rack level, Arm’s modeled performance averages 1.99X AMD’s, using power estimates of 950W, 1,050W, and 1,700W for the two Arm configurations and AMD’s EPYC 9755. The comparison includes seven workloads spanning tooling, agentic workflows, and reasoning/planning, with results calculated using normalized performance ratios. Arm’s methodology focuses on representative agent tasks, repeatable CPU measurements, and validation against end-to-end task outcomes, such as database transaction speeds. The tests used different software environments, with Arm employing custom Linux builds and AMD using Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux 6.8. While Arm’s AGI CPU led in most metrics, it lagged in MySQL and Milvus throughput. Signal65 confirmed the results within 0.5% but noted limitations in verifying BIOS and memory settings for Arm and EPYC 9755 systems. AMD and Nvidia use different benchmarks, with AMD emphasizing agents per watt and Nvidia highlighting single-thread performance. Arm’s findings do not establish it as the overall leader, as the results depend on specific workloads and configurations. The industry lacks a unified benchmarking standard, with AMD’s latest EPYC 9006 “Venice” family also targeting agentic AI.

item.title: Baseus releases security camera with spotlight that tracks moving targets
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Baseus’ new security camera has a spotlight that tracks and follows moving targets
Baseus unveiled the Security PrimeSentinel U2 Pro Outdoor 3K Dual Camera, featuring a motorized spotlight that tracks and illuminates moving targets. The spotlight enhances video clarity in low light and deters intruders by directly targeting them. The camera pairs two 3K sensors: one for fixed-area monitoring and another with 360-degree zoom, tilt, and pan capabilities. Full-color night vision aids in identifying people, animals, or vehicles. AI-powered motion detection differentiates between people, pets, vehicles, and activities like package deliveries, while ignoring irrelevant movements like wind-blown branches. Footage is stored locally on a 512GB encrypted memory card and accessible via Baseus’ mobile app or smart home devices. The camera installs in about two minutes using wall or ceiling mounts, connects wirelessly to a home network, and operates on a rechargeable battery lasting up to 150 days. A 3W solar panel can extend battery life with 40 minutes of sunlight. The U2 Pro is priced at $269.99 in the U.S. and €269.99 in Europe, with European availability starting October 15. Baseus claims the spotlight improves detection and identification while reducing false alerts. The camera’s design balances proactive deterrence with user-friendly features for after-hours activities like nighttime pet care.

item.title: User switches from Premiere Pro to Codex with open-source tools
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: I stopped using Premiere Pro to edit videos—Codex can do it for me using free open-source tools
A user transitioned from Adobe Premiere Pro to Codex, using free open-source tools for video editing. Codex handles basic tasks like importing clips, trimming, arranging footage, and exporting timelines through natural language prompts. It leverages FFmpeg for file manipulation and Pillow for adding text overlays. The user tested Codex's ability to trim speech, adjust audio levels, apply fades, and create color corrections, achieving results comparable to manual editing. For advanced features like 3D text titles, Codex used Blender and OpenCV. The user also tested automatic subtitle generation with Whisper. While not a full replacement for Premiere Pro, Codex demonstrated capabilities across multiple editing functions. The user noted that other open-source tools like Kdenlive, Shotcut, and Audacity could offer additional features through scripting, though GUI automation is more complex. The experience highlights that AI-driven tools can perform many editing tasks without requiring traditional software clones.

item.title: iPhone Duo Launch May Face Stock Shortages Due to Supply Issues
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Wanna Pick Up an iPhone Duo on Launch Day? It May Be Harder Than You Think
Apple’s upcoming iPhone Duo, priced at $2,000 starting, may face significant stock shortages on its Oct. 23 launch day. MacRumors reports Apple Store employees have been instructed to discourage walk-in buyers from expecting to purchase the device, as no inventory is likely available for in-store purchases. The advisory’s global applicability remains unclear, with potential regional variations in availability. Supply chain challenges have plagued the iPhone Duo’s production, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who noted the issues are more severe than Apple initially anticipated. Earlier this month, Apple nearly delayed the launch to late November but secured enough inventory to proceed with the October release. Production slowed to just a few hundred units per day in September, as reported by Nikkei Asia, due to the company’s stringent quality control standards. These constraints suggest customers may struggle to obtain the device on launch day, despite Apple’s confidence in consumer demand.

item.title: Mozilla Accuses Microsoft of Forcing Edge as Default Browser
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Mozilla Is Calling Out Microsoft for Forcing Edge on Users, and It's Absolutely Right
Mozilla is accusing Microsoft of using dark patterns to force Edge as the default browser on Windows 11, citing practices like pre-checked options in setup pop-ups that make Edge the default. Mozilla’s counsel Kush Amlani claims Microsoft has not met its 2023 promise to adopt a 'principled approach' to browser defaults. The company’s tactics, such as the 'Let’s finish setting up your PC' screen with an enabled-by-default Edge option, have drawn criticism from Mozilla and others. European regulations now require Microsoft to respect user choices, making the Start menu open links in the default browser instead of Edge. Amlani argues Microsoft could improve if forced by governments or public pressure, but current dissatisfaction remains insufficient. Mozilla also highlights broader concerns about tech giants like Apple and Google, which similarly prioritize their own browsers and ecosystems. Apple’s iOS restricts third-party browsers globally, while ChromeOS and Googlebook OS rely heavily on Chrome. Mozilla’s Ajit Varma notes these companies aim to steer users toward their own services, creating closed ecosystems. The organization calls for Microsoft to release the European Windows version worldwide and urges users to push for change. Mozilla claims many users are unaware their default browser has been switched, with some reporting lost bookmarks after defaults changed to Edge.

item.title: Google links phone numbers to all accounts on Android devices
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google is linking your phone number to accounts you wanted to keep separate
Google is automatically linking phone numbers on Android devices to every Google account signed in on that device, including secondary work accounts and alternate profiles. Users report receiving surprise verification emails from noreply-phone-verification@google.com without explicitly opting in. The feature, intended to ensure services like account recovery and RCS messaging function properly, requires no explicit consent and links phone numbers to all accounts on the device. Users can disable automatic verification in Settings > Google > All services > Phone number verification, but some report the setting reactivates on its own. Disabling the feature does not remove existing links, which must be manually deleted from individual accounts via the Google Account’s Personal Info page. Google cites practical reasons for the design but has not addressed concerns about informed consent or provided clarity on why the change was implemented. Android Central has sought comment from Google but has not yet received a response. Users who maintain separate accounts for personal, work, or disposable profiles face challenges keeping phone numbers isolated, as the system does not distinguish between account types. The default-on nature of the feature raises questions about user control over personal data, with some advocating for more transparent opt-in processes.

item.title: Apple HomeView Delayed for Over a Year Due to AI Issues
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Apple’s HomeViews Reportedly Collected Dust in Warehouses ‘For the Better Part of a Year’
Apple’s HomeView smart home device, set to launch next month, has been sitting in warehouses for nearly a year due to delays in developing its AI-powered software. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that the product was frozen for months as Apple struggled to refine its AI interface, eventually renting an AI model from Google to expedite progress. The device’s hardware, including an A18 processor and 8GB memory, is outdated by current standards, positioning it as a relic for older consumers. Gurman notes that the delay has allowed former Apple employees to reminisce about their work on the project, with one, Carl Schoeller, sharing details about optimizing screen brightness through complex simulations. The HomeView’s release is also tied to LG’s Apple Home Collection, which includes smart home devices designed in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. However, LG’s recent privacy controversies—following claims that its smart TVs continuously record ambient audio—have complicated the launch timing, as Apple now faces potential reputational risks linked to its partner. The company’s struggles with AI development and supply chain coordination highlight broader challenges in integrating advanced technology into consumer products.

item.title: Overclocker breaks 12-year Cinebench record with ancient hardware
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Cinebench world record that stood for 12 years gets toppled
Overclocker Luumi broke a 12-year Cinebench R11.5 record using an Intel Core i5 4670K processor. The system, built with DDR3 RAM, LN2 cooling, and a Corsair AXi 1600 power supply, achieved a multicore score of 10.8 cb. The record, previously held by a Haswell-era CPU, was surpassed by Luumi’s overclocked 4670K running at 6,301.00 MHz. The achievement highlights that high-performance overclocking is possible with older hardware, as the system used an ASRock Z97 OC Formula motherboard and XPG DDR3 memory. While the score isn’t the highest for all quad-core processors, it remains the best for the Core i5 4670K category. A modern laptop with a 12C/24T CPU outperformed the 4670K in benchmark tests, but the older Cinebench version still runs on Windows 11. The result underscores that legacy benchmarks remain functional on modern systems, unlike some older tests that fail on newer hardware. Luumi’s success also marks a rare overclocking feat on HWBot without requiring cutting-edge components like X3D CPUs or RTX 5090 GPUs.

item.title: TT Nature Bird Feeder: Two-Week Review Shows Value and Setup Challenges
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: TT Nature bird feeder review: two weeks with the budget wooden smart feeder camera
The TT Nature Bird Feeder Station is a budget-friendly wooden smart feeder with a 1080p camera, designed for casual birdwatchers. It features FSC-certified natural timber construction, a dark metal roof, and an included solar panel, offering a rustic aesthetic suitable for traditional garden setups. Unlike competitors like Birdfy and Bird Buddy, which use custom software, TT Nature employs off-the-shelf hardware paired with third-party apps, resulting in a simpler but less polished user experience. The feeder’s physical build is sturdy and easy to assemble, with mounting hardware for trees, walls, or fences. However, the app setup proved challenging, requiring manual configuration and temporarily switching the router to a 2.4GHz band. Once connected, Wi-Fi remains stable, though motion detection is slow, often capturing only the tail end of bird visits. Video quality is sharp but lacks detail for feather identification, and the camera lens fogged during damp mornings. Storage options include microSD cards (up to 128GB) and free 3-day cloud storage, but AI bird identification requires a subscription. The feeder’s solar-powered design and minimal maintenance make it a cost-effective option at around $140, though its basic app and setup hurdles may deter some users. While not ideal for capturing every bird visit, it offers reliable performance for casual use and blends naturally into outdoor spaces.

item.title: Windows 11 Gets App Launch Speed Boost in Preview Build
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Windows 11 is getting what should be a hefty speed boost for apps
Microsoft is testing a performance update for Windows 11 that accelerates app launches, starting with Microsoft Edge. The latest Release Preview build routes requests for Edge to an already-running instance instead of launching a new process, reducing launch time for subsequent openings. A 'cold' first launch remains slower, but repeated use benefits from the optimization. Microsoft plans to expand this capability to other Windows 11 apps, though third-party developers may take time to adopt the feature. The update builds on existing improvements like preloading for Edge and File Explorer, and the Low Latency Profile feature. Analysts note the delay in addressing performance issues, as Windows 11 faced complaints about sluggishness since its release. Microsoft only prioritized fixes this year after user backlash over AI features and ongoing performance problems. Critics argue the company could have addressed these issues earlier but delayed action until user frustration reached a critical point. The update reflects a shift toward prioritizing performance, though challenges like reliable updates and stability remain unresolved. Microsoft's approach to future operating systems will be tested by whether it applies this proactive optimization strategy to avoid similar delays.

item.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Expands Night City’s Story but Falls Short of First Season’s Impact
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Night City Doesn’t Burn Quite as Brightly the Second Time in ‘Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2’
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, the sequel to the acclaimed Netflix series, expands its dystopian world of Night City but falls short of the first season’s emotional and narrative impact. The show, written by Bartosz Sztybor and directed by Kai Ikarashi, follows four protagonists—Roman Carax, D, Weak Kingsley, and Talia—whose intersecting stories explore themes of ambition, corruption, and survival. Unlike the first season’s focus on David Martinez’s tragic journey, this season shifts to a more ensemble-driven narrative, weaving together corporate conspiracies, gang conflicts, and personal struggles. The series draws inspiration from films like Pulp Fiction, Léon, and Blade Runner, blending stylish visuals with a gritty, raw aesthetic. While praised for its ambitious scope and character depth, the show struggles with pacing, relying on montages and time jumps that dilute its momentum. Critics note that the narrative’s complexity—aiming to bridge the first season and the video game’s plot—often feels overstretched, leaving characters’ motivations underdeveloped. Despite these flaws, the series remains a compelling vertical slice of the Cyberpunk universe, offering a darker, more expansive take on Night City’s chaos. However, it fails to match the emotional resonance of its predecessor, leaving viewers with a sense of unfinished potential.

item.title: Ember launches temperature-controlled Mug 3 with app-free temperature adjustments
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Ember’s new temperature-controlled mug makes my nightly tea ritual even better
Ember released its third-generation smart mug, the Mug 3, designed to maintain drink temperatures without requiring app interaction. The mug features a bottom-mounted button to cycle through five preset temperatures, starting at 125°F and increasing by 5°F increments up to 145°F. Users can adjust temperatures without accessing their phone, a change welcomed for those experiencing app connectivity issues. However, the button’s placement on the bottom of the mug is criticized for being inconvenient when handling hot liquid, requiring firm presses and tilting. The app still allows customization, with recommended temperatures for black coffee, green tea, and lemon water, plus user-defined presets. Additional upgrades include a sliding lid to prevent spills, up to three hours of temperature maintenance on a single charge, and dishwasher-safe construction. The Mug 3 is available in 10-ounce ($129) and 14-ounce ($149) sizes with multiple color options. Ember also launched the Tumbler 2, a 16-ounce alternative to previous models, priced at $179. Both products are available on Ember’s website, Target, and Amazon.

item.title: CoreWeave's debt crisis sparks AI industry-wide concerns
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
CoreWeave's bonds have slipped into distressed territory, requiring investors to demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than government bonds. Chamath Palihapitiya raised concerns about the AI buildout being a private credit bubble, prompting a 20% drop in CoreWeave's shares and collateral damage in other AI stocks. The company owes over $35 billion in debt, much of it from GPU-backed loans, and has not turned a profit despite its role in providing compute power. Investors fear CoreWeave's ability to repay as more supply enters the market, with John Yovanovic of MetLife noting the industry faces another 18 months of supply. CoreWeave's $103.7 billion in remaining performance obligations, largely from Microsoft, OpenAI, and Nvidia, provides temporary stability, though OpenAI's financial health remains uncertain. The company's debt concerns have spilled over to other AI firms, including Oracle, which saw a 10% share drop and bond sell-offs. CoreWeave's situation highlights broader risks in the neocloud sector, where reliance on high-debt models and uncertain revenue streams threaten long-term viability.

item.title: Ahrefs Brand Radar Analyzes AI Visibility and Competitor Data
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Ahrefs Brand Radar review
Ahrefs Brand Radar allows users to analyze AI visibility and competitor data by comparing brands across platforms like ChatGPT and Perplexity. The tool provides insights into mentions, citations, and estimated impressions, enabling users to track brand sentiment and visibility trends. However, the full AI index costs $699/month, with limited allowances for custom prompts. The reviewer tested the platform by comparing Saily eSIM with competitors Airalo and Holafly, noting that while the data offers depth, estimated impressions and manual verification are required. Custom Prompts allow users to define specific questions, though they consume allowances quickly, especially for platforms like Claude, which use eight checks per execution. The tool’s AI Share of Voice metric depends on selected brands and filters, and its sentiment analysis report highlights positive vs. negative mentions. While the index is useful for agencies researching multiple brands, smaller businesses may find the cost prohibitive without a clear plan. The reviewer recommends using Custom Prompts for targeted questions and emphasizes the need to verify results, as cited pages don’t guarantee AI recommendations. Additional reports cover YouTube, Reddit, and TikTok, but they come with separate access conditions. Overall, Brand Radar offers valuable depth for competitive research but requires careful use due to its complexity and cost.

item.title: Final releases 40-gram wireless headphones with basic features
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: It’s hard to imagine wireless headphones ever getting lighter than these
Final, a Japanese headphone maker, has released the Porta, claiming to be the lightest wireless headphones available. Weighing just 40 grams, the on-ear design uses a single wire structure for minimal weight, contrasting with Marshall’s Milton A.N.C., which weighs 200 grams. The Porta offers up to eight hours of battery life via a 57mAh USB-C chargeable battery. Available for preorder at 12,800 yen ($80) with black or orange ear pads, shipping begins October 23. The design resembles Sony’s vintage Walkman headphones but lacks active noise cancellation, relying instead on an IPX4 rating for water resistance. Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity supports SBC and AAC codecs for audio streaming. The Porta is sold through Final’s online store and an Amazon shop for U.S. customers, though not yet listed on Amazon. Functionality remains basic, with no advanced features beyond wireless pairing and moisture resistance.

item.title: PlayStation 6 Could Cost Over $1,000 Due to High Component Costs
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: PlayStation 6 may cost over $1,000 as leaker predicts huge component costs
A leaker named KeplerL2 claims the PlayStation 6’s storage and memory alone could cost $680, potentially pushing the console’s total bill of materials past $1,000. This prediction aligns with earlier estimates from July 2026, which forecasted a $960 cost for components, now likely higher due to rising hardware prices. The AI-driven RAM crisis has driven up component costs, affecting everything from graphics cards to smartphones, and PlayStation 6 components like memory, storage, and GPU are among the priciest. Sony has stated it does not intend to sell hardware at significant losses, suggesting the final price could approach the $1,000 mark. KeplerL2, a known leaker with past credibility in console and hardware predictions, warned that escalating costs could make the PlayStation 6 one of the most expensive consoles ever. Sony has not commented on pricing, but its plan to phase out physical discs adds to concerns about future costs for gamers. The situation highlights the ongoing impact of supply chain issues on consumer electronics pricing.

item.title: Uncontrolled IT Changes Pose Security and Compliance Risks
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Change is constant across your IT estate. But is it under control?
IT teams face growing challenges managing constant changes across their infrastructure, which can lead to security risks, system failures, and compliance issues. Unmanaged changes, such as automatic patches or rushed upgrades, create vulnerabilities that enable over 90% of cyber incidents investigated. Director at Cloudhouse highlights that without proper oversight, systems drift from their intended baseline, increasing the likelihood of outages and attacks. Organizations must monitor vast, complex IT estates with hundreds or thousands of endpoints, where automated and external changes often go unnoticed. To address this, three key steps are recommended: first, using automation tools for real-time drift detection to establish a known-good configuration baseline. Second, automating change approval processes to validate detected changes against approved baselines and reduce manual errors. Third, ensuring continuous compliance with auditable trails to meet regulatory requirements and expedite incident response. Effective change management not only mitigates risks but also accelerates innovation and improves system resilience. As AI and cloud tools expand, controlling change remains critical to prevent damaging incidents and maintain operational stability.

item.title: Homeowner uses 3D-printed switches to make smart home more accessible
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: These 3D-printed wall switches made my Home Assistant smart home feel more accessible
A homeowner needed to make their smart home more accessible for guests. They used a 3D printer to create custom wall switch covers that fit over existing switches, allowing IKEA remotes to function as smart controls. The setup integrates with Home Assistant via Zigbee, enabling scenes like 'Focus' and 'Relax' through smartphone or voice commands. The temporary solution involves removing switch faceplates and using Blu-Tack to secure the covers, with gray filament chosen for aesthetics. The homeowner plans to replace old switches with more advanced systems eventually but sees the 3D-printed covers as a cost-effective interim fix. They also aim to design an HVAC control system using a tablet or display, with a 3D-printed enclosure planned for the setup.

item.title: Even Realities G2 smart glasses face control issues despite hardware upgrades
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Even Realities G2 review: Smart glasses, stupid controls
Even Realities' G2 smart glasses offer improved specs over the G1, including a higher resolution (640 x 350), faster refresh rate (60Hz), and better brightness (1,200 nits). The device is IP65-rated for water and dust, with a larger battery and four microphones. A new smart ring, priced at $249, serves as a control interface but faces usability issues. The ring's small touchpad struggles to distinguish gestures like taps, swipes, and long presses, leading to accidental app openings. While the display improvements allow smooth scrolling and real-time notifications, the control scheme complicates the user experience. The G2 also includes features like translation, navigation, and a productivity score tracking wellness metrics. However, the app ecosystem remains niche, with limited third-party apps. Competitors like Xgimi's MemoMind One and RayNeo's iO offer similar features, including alternative control methods like a watch-style crown. Despite its flaws, the G2 represents progress in smart glasses, though its control system remains a significant hurdle.

item.title: US Fossil Fuel Infrastructure Surpasses Decade-Highs Amid Renewables Slowdown
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: The fossil fuel comeback is here
The US is constructing more fossil fuel infrastructure than in a decade while renewable energy growth slows, according to a report by the Environmental Defense Fund and Atlas Public Policy. Electricity demand is rising faster than in over a decade due to data centers, factories, and electric vehicles. The Trump administration has prioritized fossil fuels over renewables, issuing stop work orders, blocking permits, and removing tax incentives for wind and solar projects. Despite this, solar and wind generated more electricity than coal for the first time in 2024, with solar accounting for 81% of new capacity. Fossil fuel projects now make up 30% of new capacity, up from 5% in 2024, and could reach 70% of the development pipeline by 2030. Planned fossil fuel capacity would hit 68 gigawatts by 2030, a 45% increase from six months prior. Renewable projects are being canceled at a faster rate than fossil fuels, with 4.9% of solar/wind projects canceled versus 2.9% for fossil fuels. New solar and wind farms remain cheaper than gas, costing $68–$69 per megawatt-hour compared to $90 for natural gas. Fossil fuels also face price volatility and contribute to air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions, driving up electricity bills. The report warns that completing fossil fuel projects could lock in higher pollution and electricity prices for decades.
